senses.gloss: a stranger. Tanḥ. Vayigg. 4 גרא שנעשה ג׳ he is named Gera, because he (Joseph) became a stranger, v. גּוּר.—Esp. a proselyte, convert to Judaism.
units: <cite ref="Yevamot 46b:17">Yeb. 46ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Berakhot 47b:12">Ber. 47ᵇ</cite> <he>לעולם אינו ג׳ וכ׳</he> one is not a proselyte until he has been &c. Yeb. l. c.; <cite ref="Kiddushin 62b:1">Kidd. 62ᵇ</cite> <he>ג׳ צריך שלשה</he> a proselyte requires a court of three for making declaration and immersion.

<cite ref="Mishnah Keritot 2:1">Kerith. II, 1</cite> <he>ג׳ מחוסר כפרה</he> a proselyte who has not yet offered a sacrifice in the Temple; a. v. fr.—<he>ג׳ צֶדֶק</he> a full, true proselyte, <he>ג׳ תּוֹשָׁב</he> one who, for the sake of acquiring limited citizenship in Palestine, renounces idolatry.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 96b:8">Snh. 96ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Gittin 57b:6">Gitt. 57ᵇ</cite>; a. fr.—<he>ג׳ שקר</he> an insincere proselyte (from impure motives).

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Bava Metzia 5:5:4">Y. B. Mets. V, 10ᶜ</cite>.—Pl. <cite ref="C01351"><he>גֵּרִים</he></cite>, constr. <he>גֵּרֵי</he>, <cite ref="C00830"><he>גֵּירֵי</he></cite>.—<he>ג׳ גרורים</he> self-made converts, not formally admitted.
Ab. Zar. 3ᵇ; 24ᵃ; a. e.—גרי אריות lion-proselytes, i.e. proselytes from mere fear (with ref. to II Kings XVII, 25 sq.).

<cite ref="Kiddushin 75b">Kidd. 75ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Sanhedrin 85b:24">Snh. 85ᵇ</cite>; a. fr.—<he>גרי חלומות</he> proselytes converted by the advice of a dreamer or an interpreter of dreams; <he>גרי מרדכי ואסתר</he> such as joined the Jewish ranks from motives like those prevalent in the days of Mordecai and Esther (<cite ref="Esther 8:17">Esth. VIII, 17</cite>).

<cite ref="Mishnah Niddah 7:3">Nidd. VII, 3</cite> (<cite ref="Niddah 56b:37">56ᵇ</cite>) <he>גרים טועין</he> Ar. (ed. <he>וטועין</he>) proselytes not living in accordance with the Jewish usages.—<he>בן גרים</he> a descendant of proselytes.
<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Metzia 4:10">B. Mets. IV, 10</cite> (<cite ref="Bava Metzia 58b:8">58ᵇ</cite>).—
<cite ref="Shabbat 33b:5">Sabb. 33ᵇ</cite> <he>יהודה בן ג׳</he>. [Mode of admission, v.
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 8:9">Num. R. s. 8</cite>; <cite ref="Niddah 13b:22">Nidd. 13ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Pesachim 87b:14">Pes. 87ᵇ</cite>; a. fr.]. Fem. <cite ref="C01320"><he>גֵּרָה</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 88:7">Gen. R. s. 88</cite>, end.—Usu. <cite ref="C00668"><he>גִּיּוֹרֶת</he></cite>.
